assessment: The UK Biobank questionnaire uses apricot as an example in a combined dried-fruit count. Genetic proxies were evaluated against low back pain case status outside a Parkinson cohort. No separate apricot or pain severity estimate appears.
Orange denotes week 12 in the biomarker figure. The constipation events occurred during blueberry supplementation, with no orange exposure.
Two of ten participants reported constipation during blueberry powder supplementation in an uncontrolled mild cognitive impairment study. The preparation and population differ from the frozen claim.

Coffee, saffron and black cumin are questionnaire entries for perceived joint symptom change in rheumatic disease. No separately measured fatigue result for those foods appears. A discussion citation mentions fatigue in a garlic study.

The rheumatology survey lists curcumin, ginger and cloves. Its pain rating describes the cohort and the paper gives no preparation-specific pain severity estimates for these entries in people with Parkinson disease.
Resveratrol appears in red-wine discussion. The genetic analysis tests food-group and red-wine associations with Parkinson susceptibility, without a grape ingestion or muscle rigidity outcome.
